To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) static analysis of memory accesses can scale to millions of lines of C code; (2) static analysis of such code can be effective in finding real errors; and (3) static analysis of this code can be done with a low rate of false positives.

1) static analysis can effectively and automatically detect a wide range of memory access errors in large, real-world programs; 2) static analysis can automatically identify a large set of functions that are likely to contain errors and can focus its analysis on these functions; and 3) a constraint solver is a powerful and effective tool for static analysis, but it can be made more effective by using a combination of selective power and selective constraint generation.
ARCHER is a static memory access checker, that uses path-sensitive, symbolic analysis to detect memory corruption errors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding and eliminating memory access errors in large, real software systems.
the following question: can we develop a static checker that scales to large systems and finds real errors in them?
the design of effective static analyses that can be applied to large bodies of source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ARCHER is a powerful, scalable, and effective memory access checker.
ARCHER is the most effective static checker for memory access errors that is available today.
ARCHER finds a lot of errors in a lot of code and is very effective at finding errors that are exploitable as security holes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found over 2000 memory access errors in over 1,000,000,000 lines of C source code.
ARCHER finds a large number of real errors, and it does so with low overhead, low false positive rates and low maintenance costs.
ARCHER finds a large number of memory access bugs, and that it does so in large bodies of code.
The main takeaway from our work is that
static analysis can find many real, exploitable memory access errors in large, complex systems.
static analysis is a practical and powerful technique for finding memory access errors.
it is possible to build a practical, effective memory checker that scales to real code and that can find real errors.
